newsitem.title: USA: Father of Tejano star Selena sues her murderer.
newsitem.headline: Father of Tejano star Selena sues her murderer.

text.p: The father of slain Tejano singer Selena has filed a wrongful death lawsuit against the woman convicted of killing the young star, attorneys said on Monday.
The suit accuses Yolanda Saldivar of "gross negligence" in the March 31, 1995, shooting of 23-year-old Selena in a Corpus Christi hotel and asks for unspecified damages, according to court documents.
In October 1995, Saldivar was found guilty of murdering Selena and sentenced to life in prison.
Attorney Patrick McGuire, who is handling Saldivar's appeal of the conviction, told Reuters his client had no money and that he did not know what Selena's father, Abraham Quintanilla, was seeking.
Neither Quintanilla nor his attorney, Jaime Capelo, would comment. The suit was filed at the Nueces County Courthouse in Corpus Christi last month.
An attorney close to the case who asked not to be identified, said Quintanilla may be attempting to prevent Saldivar from making money off the story.
Saldivar, 36, shot Selena Quintanilla Perez to death when the singer fired her for allegedly embezzling from her clothing boutiques, prosecutors charged during her two-week trial in Houston.

She had been president of Selena's fan club, then became the manager of the boutiques where clothes designed by the singer were sold. Defence attorney Douglas Tinker argued in the trial that Saldivar, upset by accusations of theft, meant to kill herself but accidentally shot Selena in a meeting at the Corpus Christi hotel.
Selena won a 1993 Grammy for best Mexican-American album and was the queen of Tejano, a hybrid music with a huge following in the U.S.-Mexico border region.
A Warner Bros. movie about Selena's life, starring Jennifer Lopez and Edward James Olmos, was expected to be released next spring.
